arxiv-2304-13026.title: Filtrations on quantum cohomology from the Floer theory of ℂ ∗ \mathbb{C}^{*} -actions
arxiv-2304-13026.creator: Alexander F. Ritter, Filip Živanović
arxiv-2304-13026.description: Abstract . We construct a filtration by ideals on quantum cohomology for symplectic manifolds with a Hamiltonian S 1 S^{1} -action that extends to a pseudoholomorphic ℂ ∗ \mathbb{C}^{*} -action. These spaces include all Conical Symplectic Resolutions, in particular all Quiver Varieties.

arxiv-2306-09067.title: 2nd Place Winning Solution for the CVPR2023 Visual Anomaly and Novelty Detection Challenge: Multimodal Prompting for Data-centric Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2306-09067.creator: Yunkang Cao, Xiaohao Xu, Chen Sun, Yuqi Cheng, Liang Gao, Weiming Shen
arxiv-2306-09067.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yunkang Cao, Xiaohao Xu, Chen Sun, Yuqi Cheng, Liang Gao, Weiming Shen. This technical report introduces the winning solution of the team Segment Any Anomaly for the CVPR2023 Visual Anomaly and Novelty Detection (VAND) challenge. Going beyond uni-modal prompt, e.g. , language prompt, we present a novel framework, i.e. , Segment Any Anomaly + (SAA + + ), for zero-shot anomaly segmentation with multi-modal prompts for the regularization of cascaded modern foundation models.

arxiv-2411-01532.title: SPARC: SPectral ARchitectures tackling the Cold-start problem in Graph learning
arxiv-2411-01532.creator: Yahel Jacobs *, Reut Dayan *, Uri Shaham
arxiv-2411-01532.description: Abstract Graphs play a central role in modeling complex relationships in data, yet most graph learning methods falter when faced with cold-start nodes—new nodes lacking initial connections—due to their reliance on adjacency information. To tackle this, we propose SPARC, a groundbreaking framework that introduces a novel approach to graph learning by utilizing generalizable spectral embeddings.

arxiv-2411-09446.title: Note on a conjecture of Ramírez Alfonsín and Skałba Thanks: † ORCID: 0000-0001-7016-309X & \& corresponding author
arxiv-2411-09446.creator: Tianhan Dai, Yuchen Ding † and Hui Wang
arxiv-2411-09446.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tianhan Dai, Yuchen Ding † and Hui Wang. Let 2 < a < b 2<a<b be two relatively prime integers and g = a ​ b − a − b g=ab-a-b . It is proved that there exists at least one prime p ≤ g p\leq g of the form p = a ​ x + b ​ y ​ ( x , y ∈ ℤ ≥ 0 ) p=ax+by~(x,y\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}) , which confirms a 2020 conjecture of Ramírez Alfonsín and Skałba.

arxiv-2502-14405.title: Differentiable Black-box and Gray-box Modeling of Nonlinear Audio Effects
arxiv-2502-14405.creator: Marco Comunità, Christian J. Steinmetz, Joshua D. Reiss, Centre for Digital Music
arxiv-2502-14405.description: Abstract Audio effects are extensively used at every stage of audio and music content creation. The majority of differentiable audio effects modeling approaches fall into the black-box or gray-box paradigms; and most models have been proposed and applied to nonlinear effects like guitar amplifiers, overdrive, distortion, fuzz and compressor.

arxiv-2508-00194.title: AUDIO PROTOTYPICAL NETWORK FOR CONTROLLABLE MUSIC RECOMMENDATION
arxiv-2508-00194.description: Abstract Traditional recommendation systems represent user preferences in dense representations obtained through black-box encoder models. While these models often provide strong recommendation performance, they lack interpretability and controllability for users, leaving users unable to understand or control the system’s modeling of their preferences.

pmc-10695739.title: Molecular Engineering of Photosensitizers for Solid‐State Dye‐Sensitized Solar Cells: Recent Developments and Perspectives
pmc-10695739.creator: Bommaramoni Yadagiri, Ashok Kumar Kaliamurthy, Kicheon Yoo, Hyeong Cheol Kang, Junyeong Ryu, Francis Kwaku Asiam, Jae‐Joon Lee
pmc-10695739.description: Dye‐sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are a feasible alternative to traditional silicon‐based solar cells because of their low cost, eco‐friendliness, flexibility, and acceptable device efficiency. In recent years, solid‐state DSSCs (ss‐DSSCs) have garnered much interest as they can overcome the leakage and evaporation issues of liquid electrolyte systems.

pmc-11428615.title: NMGrad: Advancing Histopathological Bladder Cancer Grading with Weakly Supervised Deep Learning
pmc-11428615.creator: Saul Fuster, Umay Kiraz, Trygve Eftestøl, Emiel A M Janssen, Kjersti Engan, Brij Gupta, Nadia Nedjah, Kwok Tai Chui
pmc-11428615.description: The most prevalent form of bladder cancer is urothelial carcinoma, characterized by a high recurrence rate and substantial lifetime treatment costs for patients. Grading is a prime factor for patient risk stratification, although it suffers from inconsistencies and variations among pathologists. Moreover, absence of annotations in medical imaging renders it difficult to train deep learning models.

pmc-11579236.title: The interplay of perceptual processing demands and practice in modulating voluntary and involuntary motor responses
pmc-11579236.creator: Welber Marinovic, An T. Nguyen, Ann‐Maree Vallence, James R. Tresilian, Ottmar V. Lipp
pmc-11579236.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Understanding how sensory processing demands affect the ability to ignore task‐irrelevant, loud auditory stimuli (LAS) during a task is key to performance in dynamic environments. For example, tennis players must ignore crowd noise to perform optimally. We investigated how practice affects this ability by examining the effects of delivering LASs during preparatory phase of an anticipatory timing (AT) task on the voluntary and reflexive responses in two conditions: lower and higher visual processing loads.

pmc-12641673.title: Reuniting and Endolymphatic Duct Macrophages: Localization and Possible Roles
pmc-12641673.creator: Elisa Vivado, Daniele Cossellu, Paola Perin, Leonardo Manzari
pmc-12641673.description: Background: The inner ear hosts several macrophage populations. Endolymphatic sac macrophages can phagocytose otoconia, and spiral limbus macrophages express genes for fluid shear stress sensing and bone remodeling. Obstruction of endolymph flow by saccular otoconia could be linked to endolymphatic hydrops.

pmc-12704017.title: Integrating quantitative chemical and microbial risk assessments to optimise the disinfection of fresh products
pmc-12704017.creator: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Antonio Luciano, Alberto Garre Pérez, Pablo Fernández Escámez, Marios G. Kostakis, Nikos Thomaidis, Vasilis Valdramidis
pmc-12704017.description: The fellowship, titled ‘Integrating quantitative chemical and microbial risk assessments to optimize the disinfection of fresh products’ was implemented at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (Greece). The fellowship aimed to provide practical training on the quantitative chemical risk assessment of emulsified nano‐components used for washing fresh vegetables.

pmc-12850743.title: Endoscopic versus surgical therapies for GERD: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-12850743.creator: Ravi Teja Pasam, Karim T Osman, Babu P Mohan, Douglas G Adler
pmc-12850743.description: Background and AimsThe objective of our study was to compare the outcomes of endoscopic and surgical therapies for GERD using a network meta-analysis.MethodsOnly randomized control trials with adult patients were included in the study. Radiofrequency energy (RFe) delivery, transoral incisionless fundoplication (TIF), magnetic sphincter augmentation (MSA), and Nissen, Toupet, and anterior fundoplication were studied.

pmc-12979587.title: Interspecific interactions modulate bioturbation efficiency and nutrient dynamics in freshwater benthic communities
pmc-12979587.creator: Anupam Chakraborty, Goutam K. Saha, Gautam Aditya
pmc-12979587.description: Using the snails Filopaludina bengalensis and Gabbia orcula, along with tubificid worms and Chironomus sp., one monospecific and one combinatorial experiment were conducted in microcosms over 28 days to explore the direct and indirect interactive effects of non-predatory snails and tubificid worms on the bioturbation activity of chironomid larvae.

pmc-13543406.title: Compressive strength of endodontically treated mandibular premolars rehabilitated with three techniques: core buildup material, intraradicular fiber posts and polyethylene fibers
pmc-13543406.creator: Paula Cebada, Josefina Ingrassia, Eliana G Mamani, Sofía A Pascual, Romina Chaintiou Piorno, Pablo A Martínez, Francisco Somoza, Mariana Picca, Ariel F Gualtieri, Pablo A Rodríguez
pmc-13543406.description: The biomechanical rehabilitation of endodontically treated premolars with extensive mesio-occlusodistal (MOD) cavities is a clinical challenge due to their increased susceptibility to fracture.AimTo compare the compressive strength of endodontically treated mandibular premolars restored using different post-endodontic reconstruction protocols, using intact teeth as a reference for maximum mechanical performance.

pmc-13657460.title: Potato and warm moist compresses to accelerate healing of limb swelling and bruising after venous stent placement
pmc-13657460.creator: Qin Zhang, Zhuoyin Wang, Hongqun Zhang, Xiaojuan Han, Jiani Bao, Yaru Yang, Qi Chen
pmc-13657460.description: Rationale:Hemodialysis is an essential renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease, and an autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is preferred because of its durability and low complication rate. Maintaining AVF patency is critical for effective dialysis. AVF stenosis may reduce blood flow, impair dialysis adequacy, and compromise vascular access function.

pmc-13665946.title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
pmc-13665946.creator: Trisha Bansal, Min-Kyu Lee, Courtney Coleman, Young-Mee Kim, Dane Hintermueller, Yaner Chen, Varsha Sreekanth, Chad R. Haney, Olga A. Karginova, Raudel Avila, Jacob Matsche, Shaluah Vijeth, Farah Yousef, Kento Yamagishi, Jiheon Kang, Kaitlyn Mowry, Minsung Kim, Sophianne Loh, Sachin Clark, Huong Huy
pmc-13665946.description: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness.
